questionText:
Match the Python built-in exception in List I with its triggering operational error in List II:

List I:
(A) ZeroDivisionError
(B) IndexError
(C) KeyError
(D) ValueError

List II:
(I) Attempting integer division or modulo by zero (e.g., 10 / 0)
(II) Attempting to access a sequence index that lies outside its valid bounds (e.g., L[10] on 3-item list)
(III) Attempting to access a dictionary element using a key that does not exist in the mapping
(IV) Passing an argument of correct data type but inappropriate value (e.g., int('abc'))

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.

options.text: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
ZeroDivisionError is div by zero; IndexError is out of bounds; KeyError is missing dict key; ValueError is invalid value conversion.
Hence Option B is correct.
Hence, option (A) is the correct match.
